arxiv-2102-07602.title: Insight-HXMT observations of jet-like corona in a black hole X-ray binary MAXI J1820+070
arxiv-2102-07602.creator: Bei You, Yuoli Tuo, Chengzhe Li, Wei Wang, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Shu Zhang, Mingyu Ge, Chong Luo, Bifang Liu, Weimin Yuan, Zigao Dai, Jifeng Liu, Erlin Qiao, Chichuan Jin, Zhu Liu, Bozena Czerny, Qingwen Wu, Qingcui Bu, Ce Cai, Xuelei Cao, Zhi Chang, Gang Chen, Li Chen, Tianxiang Chen, Yibao Chen, Yong
arxiv-2102-07602.description: Abstract A black hole X-ray binary produces hard X-ray radiation from its corona and disk when the accreting matter heats up. During an outburst, the disk and corona co-evolves with each other. However, such an evolution is still unclear in both its geometry and dynamics.

arxiv-2107-13808.title: Spectral signature of mass outflow in Two Component Advective Flow Paradigm
arxiv-2107-13808.creator: Santanu Mondal ∗, Sandip K. Chakrabarti
arxiv-2107-13808.description: Abstract Outflows are common in many astrophysical systems. In the Two Component Advective Flow ( TCAF ) paradigm which is essentially a generalized Bondi flow including rotation, viscosity and cooling effects, the outflow is originated from the hot, puffed up, post-shock region at the inner edge of the accretion disk.

arxiv-2110-02705.title: Robust Multi-dimensional Model Order Estimation Using LineAr Regression of Global Eigenvalues (LaRGE)
arxiv-2110-02705.creator: Alexey A. Korobkov, Marina K. Diugurova, Jens Haueisen, Martin Haardt
arxiv-2110-02705.description: Abstract The efficient estimation of an approximate model order is very important for real applications with multi-dimensional data if the observed low-rank data is corrupted by additive noise. In this paper, we present a novel robust method for model order estimation of noise-corrupted multi-dimensional low-rank data based on the LineAr Regression of Global Eigenvalues (LaRGE).

arxiv-2111-04283.title: Gauge Parameter Independence of the Higgs Pole Mass in the Multi-Higgs model
arxiv-2111-04283.creator: Chungku Kim
arxiv-2111-04283.description: Abstract We have investigated the gauge parameter dependence of the Higgs pole masses in the multi-Higgs model in two different types of the gauge fixing conditions. It turns out that the Higgs pole masses of the multi-Higgs model when expressed in terms of the Lagrangian parameters, are independent of the gauge parameter for both cases. pacs 11.15.Bt, 12.38.

arxiv-2202-09816.title: Contextual Intelligent Decisions: Expert Moderation of Machine Outputs for Fair Assessment of Commercial Driving
arxiv-2202-09816.creator: Jimiama Mafeni Mase, Direnc Pekaslan, Utkarsh Agrawal, Mohammad Mesgarpour, Peter Chapman, Mercedes Torres Torres, Grazziela P. Figueredo
arxiv-2202-09816.description: Abstract Commercial driving is a complex multifaceted task influenced by personal traits and external contextual factors, such as weather, traffic, road conditions, etc. Previous intelligent commercial driver-assessment systems do not consider these factors when analysing the impact of driving behaviours on road safety, potentially producing biased, inaccurate, and unfair assessments.

arxiv-2205-04360.title: Distributional regression and its evaluation with the CRPS : bounds and convergence of the minimax risk The following article is a preprint version of the article. You can find the latest version of the article here : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2022.11.001 . Journal: International Journal
arxiv-2205-04360.creator: Romain Pic, Clément Dombry, Philippe Naveau, Maxime Taillardat
arxiv-2205-04360.description: Abstract The theoretical advances on the properties of scoring rules over the past decades have broadened the use of scoring rules in probabilistic forecasting. In meteorological forecasting, statistical postprocessing techniques are essential to improve the forecasts made by deterministic physical models. Numerous state-of-the-art statistical postprocessing techniques are based on distributional regression evaluated with the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS).

arxiv-2309-04747.title: When to Learn What: Model-Adaptive Data Augmentation Curriculum
arxiv-2309-04747.creator: Chengkai Hou, Jieyu Zhang, Tianyi Zhou
arxiv-2309-04747.description: Abstract Data augmentation (DA) is widely used to improve the generalization of neural networks by enforcing the invariances and symmetries to pre-defined transformations applied to input data. However, a fixed augmentation policy may have different effects on each sample in different training stages but existing approaches cannot adjust the policy to be adaptive to each sample and the training model.

arxiv-2311-13267.title: FedFN: Feature Normalization for Alleviating Data Heterogeneity Problem in Federated Learning
arxiv-2311-13267.creator: Seongyoon Kim, Gihun Lee, Jaehoon Oh, Se-Young Yun
arxiv-2311-13267.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is a collaborative method for training models while preserving data privacy in decentralized settings. However, FL encounters challenges related to data heterogeneity, which can result in performance degradation. In our study, we observe that as data heterogeneity increases, feature representation in the FedAVG model deteriorates more significantly compared to classifier weight.

arxiv-2405-20672.title: Investigating and unmasking feature-level vulnerabilities of CNNs to adversarial perturbations
arxiv-2405-20672.creator: Davide Coppola, Hwee Kuan Lee
arxiv-2405-20672.description: Abstract This study explores the impact of adversarial perturbations on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with the aim of enhancing the understanding of their underlying mechanisms. Despite numerous defense methods proposed in the literature, there is still an incomplete understanding of this phenomenon.

arxiv-2506-14475.title: The AdS Perspective on the Nonlinear Tails in Black Hole Ringdown
arxiv-2506-14475.creator: Alex Kehagias, Antonio Riotto
arxiv-2506-14475.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alex Kehagias, Antonio Riotto. Black holes gradually settle into their static configuration by emitting gravitational waves, whose amplitude diminish over time according to a power-law decay at fixed spatial locations. We show that the nonlinear tails in the presence of a quadratic source, which have been recently found to potentially dominate over the linear ones, can be simply derived from the AdS 2 × \times S 2 spacetime perspective with their amplitudes being related to the Aretakis constants.

arxiv-2511-04427.title: Does AI-Assisted Coding Deliver? A Difference-in-Differences Study of Cursor’s Impact on Software Projects Conference: arXiv Preprint; November 7; 2025
arxiv-2511-04427.creator: Hao He, Courtney Miller, Shyam Agarwal, Christian Kästner, Bogdan Vasilescu
arxiv-2511-04427.description: Abstract . Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the promise to revolutionize the field of software engineering. Among other things, LLM agents are rapidly gaining momentum in their application to software development, with practitioners claiming a multifold productivity increase after adoption. Yet, empirical evidence is lacking around these claims.

arxiv-2511-15836.title: Ab initio calculations of monopole sum rules: From finite nuclei to infinite nuclear matter
arxiv-2511-15836.creator: F. Bonaiti §, A. Porro §, S. Bacca, A. Schwenk, A. Tichai
arxiv-2511-15836.description: Abstract We compute moments of the isoscalar monopole response of N = Z N=Z closed-shell nuclei based on chiral nucleon–nucleon plus three-nucleon interactions. We employ the random phase approximation (RPA) and two ab initio many-body approaches, the in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) and coupled-cluster theory (CC).

arxiv-2512-14058.title: Real-time prediction of workplane illuminance distribution for daylight-linked controls using non-intrusive multimodal deep learning
arxiv-2512-14058.creator: Zulin Zhuang, Yu Bian
arxiv-2512-14058.description: Abstract Daylight-linked controls (DLCs) have significant potential for energy savings in buildings, especially when abundant daylight is available and indoor workplane illuminance can be accurately predicted in real time. Most existing studies on indoor daylight predictions were developed and tested for static scenes.

arxiv-2601-03602.title: 𝒏 ​ 𝒑 ↔ 𝒅 ​ 𝜸 np\leftrightarrow d\gamma reactions calculated up to 𝑬 𝜸 = 𝟐𝟎 E_{\gamma}=20 MeV

arxiv-2601-03602.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mamoon A. Sharaf, Weijie Du, Andrey M. Shirokov. We calculate the electromagnetic dipole transition cross sections for the n ​ p → d ​ γ np\rightarrow d\gamma and d ​ γ → n ​ p d\gamma\rightarrow np reactions over a broad range of energies. We use the LENPIC nucleon-nucleon interaction obtained from chiral effective field theory ( χ \chi EFT) up to next-to-next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N4LO) and effective electromagnetic dipole transition operators obtained from the same χ \chi EFT up to N2LO.

pmc-10671505.title: Healthcare Cybersecurity Ethical Concerns during the COVID-19 Global Pandemic: A Rapid Review
pmc-10671505.creator: Cristian Lieneck, Matthew McLauchlan, Sean Phillips
pmc-10671505.description: Background and objectives: Healthcare organizations have endured significant challenges and relied upon telehealth and related technological advances during the COVID-19 pandemic to allow for the sustainment of care. The purpose of this study was to systematically identify healthcare cybersecurity ethical concerns experienced during the pandemic to assist with the sustainability of the delivery of care going forward.

pmc-11534869.title: Assessment of heat tolerance and identification of miRNAs during high-temperature response in grapevine
pmc-11534869.creator: Lipeng Zhang, Yuanxu Teng, Yue Song, Junpeng Li, Zhen Zhang, Yuanyuan Xu, Dongying Fan, Lujia Wang, Yi Ren, Juan He, Shiren Song, Xiaojun Xi, Huaifeng Liu, Chao Ma
pmc-11534869.description: With global warming, heat stress has been recognized as a significant factor limiting grapevine development and fruit quality. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of small non-coding RNAs known to play crucial regulatory roles in stress resistance. Hence, there is an immediate requirement to cultivate and identify grapevine varieties that are resistant to heat and explore miRNA-mediated heat stress defense mechanisms.

pmc-13058570.title: Towards Evidence of Rigour in Empirical Deliberative Democratic Methods: Development and Piloting of the C‐JuRI Framework
pmc-13058570.creator: Emma K. Frost, Yves Saint James Aquino, Annette Braunack‐Mayer, Lucy Carolan, Stacy M. Carter
pmc-13058570.description: BackgroundDeliberative democratic methods are increasingly being used to involve the public in health policy decision‐making. These methods are rooted in deliberative democratic theory, which proposes the methods as democratic, inclusive and relevant ways to involve the public in policy decisions.

pmc-13096194.title: High-efficiency electrochemical air capture enabled by thiadiazole redox carrier with tunable gas-selective channels
pmc-13096194.creator: Jing Hou, Yingying Cheng, Tao Yan, Zhikun Liu, Peng Kang
pmc-13096194.description: Electrochemical direct air CO2 capture (eDAC) using redox carriers enables sustainable decarbonization but suffers efficiency losses from O2-induced side reactions such as oxygen reduction and carrier oxidation. We introduce a composite electrode BPT−GPL by integrating 2,5-bis(4-pyridyl)−1,3,4-thiadiazole (BPT) with ether oxygen (–O–) enriched gas permeation layer (GPL), forming a tunable gas transport channel that facilitates CO2 diffusion while limiting O2 penetration.

pmc-13166547.title: Stellate ganglion block associated with changes in depression and anxiety in idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss: A retrospective observational study
pmc-13166547.creator: Jinyoung Oh, Sungsik Park, Kyung Hwa Kwak, Dong Gun Lim, Seung Wook Hong, Younghoon Jeon
pmc-13166547.description: Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL) is often accompanied by depression and anxiety. Stellate ganglion block (SGB) is useful to treat ISSNHL by enhancing cochlear perfusion. Recently, SGB has been reported to improve depressive symptoms in posttraumatic stress disorder, but it remains unclear whether SGB can decrease depressive symptoms and anxiety in patients with ISSNHL.

pmc-13210622.title: Activity-Based Profiling of Papain-like Cysteine Proteases in Different Plant Organs During Barley Development
pmc-13210622.creator: Igor A. Schepetkin, Andreas M. Fischer
pmc-13210622.description: Papain-like cysteine proteases (PLCPs) are vital enzymes involved in plant development, acting as key regulators of processes such as seed germination, nutrient mobilization, senescence, and programmed cell death. In the present study, we analyzed active PLCPs in various barley organs, including roots, leaves, stems, and seeds at different stages of plant development.

pmc-13305982.title: P49 Interconnected AMR profiles of Escherichia coli in Nigerian live bird markets: evidence from human, poultry, and environmental sampling
pmc-13305982.creator: Annelies van Bohemen, Kennedy Chah, Ben Swift, Andrew Mead, Lucy Brunton
pmc-13305982.description: BackgroundLive bird markets (LBMs) are key points of contact between people, poultry, and the surrounding environment, creating conditions that favour the emergence and transmission of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Escherichia coli is commonly looked to as a One Health AMR indicator organism due to its widespread presence and its capacity to acquire and disseminate resistance genes.

pmc-13532119.title: Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism Before and After Transsphenoidal Surgery for Non‐Functioning Pituitary Adenoma
pmc-13532119.creator: Victor Hantelius, Gudmundur Johannsson, Sofie Jakobsson, Erik Thurin, Tobias Hallen, Thomas Skoglund, Oskar Ragnarsson
pmc-13532119.description: ObjectiveThe effect of transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) on the hypothalamic‐pituitary‐gonadal (HPG) axis in patients with non‐functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPA) is underexplored, especially in women. Our aim was to investigate the HPG axis function before and after TSS, its association with quality of life (QoL), and to identify factors that predict its recovery after TSS.DesignThis was a prospective cohort study.
